stem: Which of the following is an absolute indicator for referral for language development concerns?

options.text: No single words by 12 months of age
No two-word combinations by 24 months of age
Speaking with an unusual accent or voice quality
Limited vocabulary at 3 years of age

explanation: No two-word combinations by 24 months of age is the absolute indicator for referral. This age-based language milestone is a red flag that warrants assessment.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because absence of single words by 12 months is not the listed absolute referral indicator in this item.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because no two-word combinations by 24 months of age is identified as an absolute indicator for referral.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because an unusual accent or voice quality may be concerning, but it is not the absolute language milestone described here.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because difficulty pronouncing consonant sounds can occur in typical development and is not the absolute referral indicator asked for here.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because limited vocabulary at 3 years is not the specific absolute indicator given in this question.

source.hint: Consider the specific age-based threshold for combining words mentioned by the doctor.
